body_en: Faʻalavelave is both the event and the obligation it creates. A wedding, a funeral, a saofaʻi, a graduation, a church dedication — each is a faʻalavelave to which the aiga must contribute. Contributions take three forms: ʻie tōga, money, and food. The contribution honours the host; the host honours the giver by acknowledging publicly. Reciprocity is tracked — when the host has a faʻalavelave of their own, they will contribute in kind.
body_sm: O le faʻalavelave o le sauniga ma le tiute e faʻatupuina. O se faʻaipoipoga, maliu, saofaʻi, faʻauʻuga, faʻapaʻiaga o se falesā — o ia mea uma o ni faʻalavelave e manaʻomia ai le fesoasoani a le aiga. E tolu vaega o fesoasoani: ʻie tōga, tupe, ma meaʻai. E faʻaaloalogia e le fesoasoani le aiga e talimalo; e faʻaaloalogia foʻi e le aiga le tagata na fesoasoani i le taʻuina aloaʻia. E manatua e le aiga le fesoasoani na maua — pe a fai sā latou faʻalavelave, e toe tuʻuina atu se fesoasoani.

sections.title_sm: Ituaiga ma le mamafa o faʻalavelave
sections.body_en: Not all faʻalavelave carry the same weight. A funeral typically demands the largest contribution. A first saofaʻi, a wedding of an aigaʼs eldest, a church dedication — these are also heavy. A first birthday, a graduation — these are lighter but still meaningful. Speak to your matai to gauge what is appropriate.
sections.body_sm: E lē tutusa le mamafa o faʻalavelave uma. O le maliu e masani lava ona sili ona mamafa. O le saofaʻi muamua, o se faʻaipoipoga a le ulumatua o le aiga, o le faʻapaʻiaga o se falesā — e mamafa foʻi. O se aso fanau muamua, o se faʻauʻuga — e itiiti, ae tāua pea. Fesili i lou matai e iloa ai le mea talafeagai.

sections.title_en: The three currencies — ʻie tōga, tupe, meaʻai
sections.title_sm: Vaega e tolu — ʻie tōga, tupe, meaʻai
sections.body_en: Every faʻalavelave contribution runs on three currencies. ʻIe tōga (fine mats) carry the cultural weight — they are named, remembered, and circulate for generations. Tupe (cash) is the practical layer — it funds the umu, the tent, the hire cars. Meaʻai (food) is the immediate hospitality — pigs, taro, palusami, tinned corned beef, drinks. Different faʻalavelave weight the three differently; a funeral leans ʻie tōga, a graduation leans tupe and meaʻai.
sections.body_sm: E soʻo se fesoasoani i le faʻalavelave, e faʻavae i ni vaega e tolu. ʻIe tōga — e faʻaaloalogia i le aganuʻu, e i ai igoa, e manatua, e faʻafesoaʻi i tupulaga e tele. Tupe — e faʻaaogāina mo le umu, faleoʻo, tāʻavale. Meaʻai — o le talimālo vave — puaʻa, talo, palusami, pisupo, mea inu. E lē tutusa le mamafa o vaega e tolu i faʻalavelave uma; e faʻamamafa e le maliu le ʻie tōga, ae faʻamamafa e le faʻauʻuga tupe ma meaʻai.

sections.body_en: Money goes in an envelope, marked with the giverʼs name and aiga. ʻIe tōga are folded carefully and laid out by a representative who names them aloud at the siʻi. Food is prepared and brought ready to serve. Hand contributions to a tulāfale of the receiving aiga or directly to the saʻo of the family — never leave them on a table unattended.
sections.body_sm: E tuʻu le tupe i totonu o se teutusi ma le igoa o le tagata ma lona aiga. E gaugau ma le faʻaaloalo ʻie tōga ma faʻaali e se sui o le igoa i le siʻi. E saunia meaʻai ma aumai ua sauni e tausi. Tuʻuina atu fesoasoani i se tulāfale o le aiga e talia po o tuʻu saʻo atu i le saʻo o le aiga — aua neʻi tuʻu i luga o se laulau.

sections.title_sm: O le talia e le aiga talimalo
sections.body_en: The receiving side is not passive. A designated tulāfale calls out each contribution as it lands — the giverʼs name, their aiga, the quantity, the ʻie tōga presented. The seated matai acknowledge with a soft mālō or fetagi. Every contribution is recorded, in memory if not on paper. To fail to name a contribution publicly is a serious slight to the giver.
sections.body_sm: E lē faʻalogologo le itu e talia. E i ai se tulāfale ua tofia e taʻuina taʻitasi le fesoasoani a ō mai — igoa o le tagata, lona aiga, le aofaʻi, ma le ʻie tōga ua faʻaali. E tali matai ua nonofo i se mālō pe fetagi. E faʻamauina soʻo se fesoasoani, i le manatu pe afai e leai i le pepa. O le lē taʻuina aloaʻia o se fesoasoani, o le lē faʻaaloalo tele lea i le tagata na foaʻi.

sections.title_sm: Pe a lē mafai ona faʻataunuʻu atoatoa
sections.body_en: If circumstance means you cannot meet the expected contribution, communicate this directly to your matai or to the receiving aiga ahead of time. Use the word faʻatoesega — apology. Send what you can with respect. To send nothing without word is the failure; to send little with explanation is honoured.
sections.body_sm: Pe afai e lē mafai ona faʻataunuʻu atoatoa le fesoasoani faʻamoemoeina, faʻailoa atu saʻo lea i lou matai po o le aiga e talia, aʻo leʻi oʻo le aso. Faʻaaogā le upu faʻatoesega. Tuʻuina atu le mea e mafai ma le faʻaaloalo. O le lē tuʻuina atu ma le lē faʻailoa — o le sese lea; o le itiiti ma le faʻamatalaga — e faʻaaloalogia.

sections.body_en: The aiga remembers. Each contribution received creates a known obligation. When that family later has their own faʻalavelave, your aiga is expected to respond. This is the rhythm of Samoan life — and the reason faʻalavelave is best understood as a long-running reciprocal relationship, not a one-off transaction.
sections.body_sm: E manatua e le aiga. E tupu se tiute mai ia fesoasoani taʻitasi. Pe a oʻo i se faʻalavelave a le isi aiga, e faʻamoemoeina lou aiga e toe tuʻuina atu. O le paō lea o le olaga Sāmoa — ma o le māfuaʻaga e mālamalama ai i le faʻalavelave, o se mafutaga umi e faʻafesoasoani, ae le o se faʻatauga e tasi.

sections.body_en: Obligations do not die with the person who accepted them. A funeral contribution your grandfather received in 1972 may be re-paid to that familyʼs grandchild in a wedding tomorrow. The aiga potopoto passes the ledger down. Younger matai learn who the aiga owes, and who owes the aiga, from the elders. This memory — a living register of who has stood with whom — is the actual mechanism of the faʻamatai.
sections.body_sm: E lē maliu tiute i le tagata na talia. O se fesoasoani na maua e lou tamā mātua i se maliu i le 1972, e mafai ona toe totogi atu i le atalii o le aiga i se faʻaipoipoga i le aso a taeao. E tuʻuina atu e le aiga potopoto le lisi i tupulaga tupu aʻe. E aʻoaʻoina matai talavou e le ʻautoeaina o ai e nofoia se tiute i le aiga, ma o ai foʻi e nofoia se tiute a le aiga. O lenei manatuaga — o le lisi o loʻo ola pea o soo o soo — o le mea moni tonu lea o le faʻamatai.

sections.title_sm: Mo i latou o loʻo nofo i fafo
sections.body_en: Distance does not end faʻalavelave. Many diaspora Samoans send money via aiga in country; others fly back for weddings and funerals. Speak to your matai or saʻo about your obligations and capacity. Do not let silence speak for you — speak openly. Many aiga will adjust expectations for those overseas when communication is good.
sections.body_sm: E lē mavae le faʻalavelave i le mamao. E tele tagata Sāmoa o loʻo nonofo i fafo e tuʻuina atu tupe e ala i aiga i Sāmoa; o nisi e folau atu i faʻaipoipoga ma maliu. Talanoa i lou matai po o le saʻo e uiga i au tiute ma le mafai. Aua le tuʻu i le filemu e tautala mo oe — talanoa lava. E tele aiga e fetuunaʻi faʻamoemoega mo i latou i fafo pe a lelei le talanoaga.
